y-m-80-11.title: If you stack 12 perfect fifths, do you get exactly octaves?
y-m-80-11.topic: Musical scales and powers: do stacked fifths meet octave?

Pitch can be expressed by frequency; pitches compare by frequency ratio. A perfect fifth has ratio 3:2 (upper note 1.5 times), and an octave doubles frequency. Some believe stacking 12 fifths passes through 12 notes and returns to same note 7 octaves higher.
Seou says, "(3/2) multiplied 12 times equals exactly 2 multiplied 7 times, so the keyboard closes perfectly." (3/2 is three halves; 2⁷=128.) 3 2 1.5 12 12 7 3 2 12 2 7 3 2 2 2 7 128

y-m-80-07.material:
This multiplication method used long ago. Write factors A,B in two columns. Left start A and keep halving (drop remainder) to 1; right start B and double each row. Keep rows where left odd; add corresponding right values to get A×B.
Example 23×14:
Left 23, right 14 (odd)
Left 11, right 28 (odd)
Left 5, right 56 (odd)
Left 2, right 112 (even)
Left 1, right 224 (odd)
14+28+56+224=322=23×14
Seoyun tries 26×15.

In Gregorian calendar, leap year means February has 29 days. Rules: ① divisible by 4 = leap year. ② Among those, divisible by 100 = common year. ③ Among those, divisible by 400 is leap again.

y-m-80-06.s.s1.r.b: You think no exceptions because cycle repeats every 4 years.
y-m-80-06.s.s1.o.c: Leap year na calendar convention, so number test can't check it.
y-m-80-06.s.s1.r.c: You miss leap years follow fixed rules; test conditions numerically.
y-m-80-06.s.s1.o.d: Only 3 similar years checked. Test other types, like multiples of 100.
y-m-80-06.s.s1.r.d: Find and test years different from those already checked.
y-m-80-06.s.s1.explain: None of three years divisible by 100. Checking same type can't show whether rule fails for other types.

y-m-80-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Year must be natural number 1600 to 2400.
y-m-80-06.s.s2.ok.c2: Jia rule says this year leap.
y-m-80-06.s.s2.fail.c2: This year not divisible by 4, so Jia rule doesn't call it leap either.
y-m-80-06.s.s2.ok.c3: Actual rule calls it common year; Jia rule is wrong here.

y-m-80-06.s.s3.hint.1: Apply rules ①–③ in order; write expression adding/subtracting counts.

y-m-80-12.topic: Lunar calendar leap-month rule and Metonic cycle
y-m-80-12.goal: Use fact lunar month ~29.53 days and year ~365.24 aren't whole-number multiples: estimate leap-month proportion, compare accumulated error and choose better rule with reasons.
y-m-80-12.material:
Lunar calendar month follows Moon cycle ~29.53059 days. Seasons must align with Sun-year ~365.2422 days. 12 months=12×29.53059≈354.367 days, about 10.9 days short yearly. So add month every few years ('leap month'). If add k leap months in n years, calendar days=(12n+k)×29.53059; season days=n×365.2422.
Minjae says, "Add leap month once every 3 years, that'll match close enough."
